introduction.problem_before: A caller that must not retry used send_once(), next to send().
introduction.change: send_once() is removed; send() is the only entry point and always retries. Side effect: no way is left to send without retry.
introduction.example_before_after: Before: send() and send_once(). After: only send(), which always retries.

steps.title: send_once() removed
steps.called_by: callers that must not retry (none left in this repository)
steps.why: One entry point instead of two.

annotations.text: No way is left to send a request exactly once (see flow 1, step 5).

scenario: The SDK no longer builds when it updates to this version.
flag.not_checked: The SDK's current code was not read.

annotations.text: Potential repeat of a request that must run once:

scenario: A caller used send_once() for a request that must run at most once.
send_once() is removed, and send() is the only call left.
send() retries on timeout, so the request may run twice.

assessment.headline: A downstream developer gets a compile error; a user of broadcast_tx loses the only no-retry path.
assessment.reason: Public API removal with a known downstream user; ties to the double-send question.
assessment.basis_note: Read: 2 files, searched this repository and the stacked PR title
assessment.smallest_correction: Keep send_once (or add a per-call retry opt-out) until the SDK has moved.
